# Connectors

<!-- purpose: Where Connectors files live, the kinds they hold and every key they accept -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Assembly connectors, each joining one component's `provide` port to another component's `require` port over a compatible interface.

One file per `connector`, in `connectors/` under the model root, named after its `name` and ending in `.yaml`. Where that file name is already taken by another element's file — compared without regard to case — the file gets the nearest free `~1`, `~2`, … instead; the element is identified by the `name` inside the file, never by its file name.

## `connector` { #connector }

<!-- purpose: Writing `connector` files in Connectors: each key, its type and default -->

One assembly connector: it links the `from` endpoint, which must be a `provide` port, to the `to` endpoint, which must be a `require` port, and the `to` port's interface must be satisfied by the `from` port's. Connector names are unique across the layer, and so is each `(from, to)` link.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The connector's identity; the file is named from it (`connectors/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the layer, must not be empty, and immutable. |
| `from` | a `connector_endpoint` block | yes | — | The providing endpoint: the component and the `provide` port the connector starts from. Its port's interface must satisfy the `to` port's, which the same interface always does. |
| `to` | a `connector_endpoint` block | yes | — | The requiring endpoint: the component and the `require` port the connector delivers to. Its port's interface must be satisfied by the `from` port's, which the same interface always does. |
| `composition` | string, the `name` of [compositions](compositions.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared composition this connector belongs to. Absent means the root composition: the root's name is a property of the model rather than a constant, so it is resolved where the model is in hand — in the writer, in the rules and in the importer — and never written into the file as a default. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the connector. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |

## Blocks used inside those files { #blocks-used-inside-those-files }

<!-- purpose: The blocks nested inside Connectors files, which are not files of their own -->

These are not files of their own: each appears as a block inside an element of this layer.

### `connector_endpoint` { #connector_endpoint }

<!-- purpose: Writing `connector_endpoint` blocks in Connectors: each key, its type and default -->

One end of an assembly connector: the component or composition type that owns the port, and the port. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change. It names the TYPE either way; the writer resolves that type to the member of it inside the connector's own composition, which is why a type may stand only once per composition.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `swc` | string, the `name` of [swc](swc.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared software component that owns the endpoint's port. Exactly one of `swc` and `composition` is set; this one is the endpoint of an ordinary component. |
| `composition` | string, the `name` of [compositions](compositions.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared composition that owns the endpoint's port, where the endpoint is a sub-composition's boundary port. Exactly one of `swc` and `composition` is set; an endpoint declaring neither, or both, is refused. |
| `port` | string | yes | — | The name of a port of that component. Must not be empty; the port's existence and its direction are checked against the component. |
